summary: Locate winding, normal, intersection and triangulation problems in both Blender source geometry and the delivered runtime primitive without treating wireframe as proof of validity.
objective: A reported defect names the asset revision, source object or glTF node and primitive, diagnostic mode, affected element and whether it exists before or after evaluation/export.
applies_when: A mesh shows holes, black faces, lighting seams, unstable n-gons or unexpected post-export triangles.
intent_signals: find flipped normals after glTF export
wireframe looks fine but mesh has a hole
locate intersecting triangles by source object
example_prompts: Add a temporary inspection mode for flipped faces and exported triangle boundaries.
Trace a shading crack from a runtime primitive back to the Blender source object.
not_for: A permanent wireframe visual style with no diagnostic question.

principles: Inspect the representation that can fail: editable Blender mesh, evaluated export mesh and loaded runtime primitive are related but not identical.
Separate topology from shading. Triangle boundaries and edge incidence expose connectivity; face orientation and vertex-normal views expose direction and smoothing; neither substitutes for the other.
Wireframe can reveal tessellation but cannot alone prove closedness, manifoldness, winding consistency or absence of coincident and intersecting faces.
Diagnostics are reversible views. They identify elements and provenance without changing authoritative geometry, normals or material state.
implementation: In Blender, inspect Face Orientation, seam/sharp markers, vertex or face indices and selected normals on the relevant source and evaluated state. Use Mesh Analysis only for the specific modes and limits it documents.

Export a frozen diagnostic revision with stable object keys. Record modifier state and triangulation ownership so a runtime triangle can be traced to the evaluated object even when edit-mode n-gons are gone.
At runtime, isolate one glTF node and primitive; draw a disposable edge or normal overlay from its actual position/index/normal buffers and label node, primitive and triangle or vertex index.

Compute explicit checks only when needed: boundary and non-manifold edge incidence, duplicate positions under a declared tolerance, degenerate triangle area, finite unit normals and winding-versus-normal disagreement. Keep open sheets and deliberate hard seams as stated exceptions.
Reset removes helpers and restores original material visibility without recomputing or replacing production attributes.
observable_checks: Use fixtures with one reversed triangle, one boundary, one three-face edge, one degenerate triangle and one deliberate open sheet; each is classified by the declared check rather than one generic red state.
Compare Blender source, evaluated mesh and loaded primitive counts and identifiers; a difference is attributed to a named modifier/export step or left unresolved.
Toggle normal and topology overlays independently; changing the diagnostic view does not change the production mesh, material, bounding data or selection identity.
Select a reported runtime triangle and resolve its node/primitive and best available source object; missing element-level correspondence is disclosed.

creative_affordances: Use sparse arrows, edge classes, exploded problem islands or a synchronized source/runtime inset.
Keep deliberate open surfaces and hard edges visually distinct from failures.
known_limits: Face Orientation is camera-relative visualization and typical outside-facing guidance, not proof that every surface should be closed or outward-facing.
Element-level source correspondence may be lost through modifiers, triangulation, merging or compression.
Authored source-checked diagnostic guidance; no mesh, export or renderer was inspected.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5 Face Orientation displays faces whose normal points toward the camera in blue and away from it in red as a quick orientation check; Blender Mesh Analysis separately offers intersection and distortion displays with documented limitations.
claims.scope: Blender viewport diagnostics only; typical outside-blue guidance is not a manifoldness, printability or export guarantee.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 defines NORMAL as normalized XYZ vertex normals, optional indices as the accessor that selects vertices for a primitive, and topology modes whose index-count constraints differ for points, lines and triangle forms.
claims.scope: Delivered glTF primitive attributes and topology; no edit-mode face, seam, modifier or manifold metadata is implied.
